module.purpose: Provides a reusable utility for removing plus-addressing tags from email local parts while preserving the domain.
module.summary: This module performs simple email normalization by splitting an address into local and domain portions, removing everything after the first plus sign in the local portion, and reconstructing the address. It is a synchronous, side-effect-free helper intended for callers that need a base address for comparison, lookup, or identity handling.
module.businessContext: Supports email identity normalization and deduplication where plus-tagged addresses should map to a base mailbox. Incorrect behavior can produce malformed addresses or fail to associate tagged mail with the underlying account.
functions: extractBaseEmail (~L2-6): Extracts the base local email address before plus-tagging.

units.name: extractBaseEmail

detail.name: extractBaseEmail
postconditions: Returns a string formed from the portion before the first '+' in the local part, followed by '@' and the portion after the first '@'.
invariants: Only the local part before the first '@' is considered for plus-suffix removal.
Additional '@' characters after the first one are not included in the returned domain.
edgeCases: When the local part contains '+', everything from the first '+' onward is removed.
When the email contains no '@', the domain value is undefined and the returned string uses the literal text 'undefined' after '@'.
When the email contains multiple '@' characters, only the first two split segments are used and later segments are discarded.
When the local part is empty or begins with '+', the returned local part is empty.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns the string `${baseLocalPart}@${domain}`, where baseLocalPart is the first local-part segment before '+' and domain is the second email segment after splitting on '@'.
detail.summary: Returns an email address with any plus-suffix removed from its local part while preserving the first domain segment.
